5. Any specified logarithmic-size hole subset can be refined

Fix a positive-probability coarse record and any specified $m$-site subset $S$ of its holes. Its conditional joint fine-output marginal can be sampled with error $\xi$ in

$$\boxed{
\exp(O_{\rm class}(m))\,
\operatorname{poly}_{\rm class}(n,B,\xi^{-1})
}
\tag{21}$$

worst-case bit work.

This remains true when the complete coarse record is exponentially unlikely.

To see the construction, retain the coarse effects outside $S$, put $I$ on $S$, and normalize the partial trace to obtain a conditional density $\chi_S$. Reconstruct its Pauli coefficients using rational weak probes

$$I\pm rP_i,\qquad r=\tfrac14.$$

For $U\subseteq S$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}(P_U\chi_S)
=
(2r)^{-|U|}
\sum_{s\in\{\pm1\}^{U}}
\left(\prod_{i\in U}s_i\right)
\frac{Z_s}{Z_{\rm out}}.
\tag{22}$$

All these probe boundaries retain a fixed balance margin. The ratios are evaluated from differences of logarithms using the accepted compiler. Their polarization amplification is at most $5^{|U|}$, and all Pauli coefficients require at most $7^m$ normalizer calls.

A rational positive density matrix is obtained by adding a certified small multiple of the identity to the approximate Hermitian Pauli expansion and renormalizing. This avoids an exact eigenvalue decision.

The hole effects inside $S$ are restored through

$$F_S\ge\theta^m I.$$

Hence their conditional normalization is at least $\theta^m$. Reconstructing $\chi_S$ to trace accuracy proportional to $\xi\theta^m$ pays this normalization with only exponential-in-$m$ work.

Finally, define

$$N_{i,x}=
\begin{cases}
M_i(x),&x\text{ rare},\\
\theta M_i(x),&x\text{ good}.
\end{cases}
\qquad
\sum_xN_{i,x}=F_i.$$

For the rational compiled density $\widehat\chi_S$, the prefix weights

$$w(x_1,\ldots,x_j)
=
\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[
\left(\bigotimes_{\ell\le j}N_{\ell,x_\ell}\right)
\left(\bigotimes_{\ell>j}F_\ell\right)
\widehat\chi_S
\right]
\tag{23}$$

are exactly rational, nonnegative and consistent. Dense contraction on $2^m$ dimensions and fixed-length dyadic sampling pay the full alphabet and randomness costs.

For $m=O(\log(n/\epsilon))$, this is polynomial work.

The conditioning scope is essential: this samples the marginal under the coarse record outside $S$. It does not supply a reader after fine rare outcomes have been exposed in other hole components.
